title: Row-Wave String Conversion Problem

content.problemStatement:
Task: Write the characters of s down and diagonally up across numRows rows, repeating this down-up movement until every character is placed. The task is to output the characters obtained by reading the rows from top to bottom.

If numRows is 1, or numRows is no fewer than the length of s, the result is s unchanged.
constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters (letters, digits, punctuation, symbols and spaces).
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]
notes: If numRows is 1 or numRows >= len(s), return s unchanged.
Simulate row assignment with a direction toggle (down/up) or compute positions using cycle length 2*numRows-2.
Target O(n) time and O(n) extra space (for output).

sampleTestCases.explanation: Placing the characters across three rows produces the row strings "PAHN", "APLSIIG", and "YIR". Reading those rows in order gives "PAHNAPLSIIGYIR".
With four rows, the zigzag row strings are "PINAL", "SIGYAHR", "PI", and "I". Reading from top row to bottom row gives "PINALSIGYAHRPI".
There is only one character and one row, so no rearrangement occurs and the result remains "A".

hidden.label: Three rows with exact cycle boundary
Exact cycle completion with four rows
Multiple cycles with a partial final cycle
Rows near half the string length

notes: All hidden test cases are concrete and use the documented JSON argument format.
Expected outputs are exact string matches; ensure correct escaping when printing JSON strings.

solution.approach: Two common O(n) approaches: (1) Simulate row assignment: maintain an array of strings for each row, iterate characters while toggling direction when reaching top or bottom, then concatenate rows. (2) Use cycle arithmetic: cycle = 2*numRows - 2; for each row r, append characters at indices r + k*cycle and (k+1)*cycle - r when applicable. Both run in O(n) time and O(n) space for the output.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) for the output (plus O(numRows) auxiliary for row buffers)
notes: Handle edge cases: numRows == 1 or numRows >= len(s) — return s directly.
When using cycle arithmetic, be careful to avoid duplicating characters for first and last rows.
For large numRows relative to s length, simulation with min(numRows, len(s)) rows avoids wasted buffers.

hints: If numRows is 1 or numRows >= len(s), return s immediately to avoid extra work.
Simulate the zigzag by maintaining a current row index and a direction flag; append each character to its row buffer.
Alternatively compute positions using cycle length = 2 * numRows - 2 and iterate row-by-row to build the result without per-character direction logic.
followUps: How would you modify the algorithm to stream characters (e.g., very long input) and produce output incrementally with bounded memory?
Can you adapt the cycle-based method to compute the character at a given output position without building the entire string?
What changes if the zigzag pattern used a different vertical spacing (e.g., variable row heights) — how would you generalize the mapping?
learningObjectives: Simulate traversal patterns and map indices to buckets.
Apply cycle arithmetic to transform index mappings efficiently.
Handle edge cases and design O(n) time, O(n) space string algorithms.
